title: Microfold cadence tally — latency/throughput scratchpad
content:
Objective:
Run quick iterative bench sweeps that mix low-latency steady traffic with microbursts (0.1s–1s) to observe how small prefix cache pressure + batch cadence interact. Looking for reproducible p99/p999 modes and early indicators of microfold cascades (rapid degradation clusters).

Context / why this is different:
- Most prior logs focused on large bursts or steady-state. This one explores high-frequency small bursts overlaying steady QPS (think user-typing autocomplete patterns).
- Hypothesis: when prefill + KV cache eviction cadence align with small bursts we see short-duration spikes that recover nonlinearly; they’re not just cold-starts.

Test harness summary:
- Model: quantized-7B-v2 (int8 sim), compilation: optimized-kernels (A100-like profile)
- Fleet: heterogeneous test pool (2xV100-like, 4xA100-like), routing set to round-robin by slot
- Workload: base qps=35, superimposed microbursts 120–200 qps lasting 150–600ms, Poisson arrival between bursts (λ tuned to keep avg=35)
- Request size: prefill tokens 8, gen tokens 28 (context heavy-ish)
- Prefill strategy variants: no-prefill, prefill-on-every-request, prefill-coalesced (window=20ms), prefix-cache-enabled/disabled
- Measurement: local harness collects p50,p90,p99,p999, avg latency, tail duration (time above 200ms), and throughput over sliding 1s windows

Experiment matrix (selected runs):
1) baseline (prefill-on-every-request, prefix-cache ON)
2) coalesced prefill (20ms) + prefix-cache ON
3) coalesced prefill + prefix-cache OFF
4) no-prefill + prefix-cache ON
5) no-prefill + prefix-cache OFF

Quick raw observations (aggregated across 30m runs):
- Baseline: p50=38ms, p90=72ms, p99=183ms, p999=340ms. Microbursts cause 250–400ms pockets; recovery <1s.
- Coalesced+cache ON: p50=40ms, p90=78ms, p99=210ms, p999=480ms. Slightly higher tail — explanation: batching increases queueing within 20ms window during microbursts.
- Coalesced+cache OFF: p50=46ms, p90=95ms, p99=320ms, p999=820ms. Very bad tails; cache OFF amplifies cold-prefill work when bursts hit.
- No-prefill+cache ON: p50=34ms, p90=65ms, p99=170ms, p999=290ms. Best p50/p90 but slightly higher variance initially.
- No-prefill+cache OFF: p50=42ms, p90=110ms, p99=450ms, p999=1100ms. Worst-case tails — confirms prefill/caching interplay matters.

Notable microfold cascade behavior (new term I'm using):
- Sequence: small burst hits -> coalesced prefill forms a medium batch -> runtime schedules kernel that holds GPU slot longer -> concurrent requests pile into same slot due to routing -> when kernel finishes, KV cache is partially invalidated due to slot churn -> following requests see repeated small cold-prefill penalties -> net effect is multiple consecutive high-latency samples (clustered), not a single isolated spike.
- Trigger points observed around average slot occupancy > 0.7 and prefill window >= 15ms under microburst.

ASCII sparklines (p99 over 120s window, example run):
- baseline: ▂▃▂▁▁▁▂▃▅▆▅▃▂▁▁
- coalesced+cache OFF: ▂▂▃▅▇▆▇▇▆▅▃▂▂▁

Short debugging notes from traces:
- Trace group t-20241019-1: saw repeated "prefill-miss" events at edges of burst -> correlate with routing decisions (slot flips every ~12ms)
- Kernel time distribution shows a heavy tail under coalesced batching; suspect serialization on long attention kernels for batches > 5 sequences
- Observed a small increase in TLS context switches in proxy when bursts occur; could add jitter to proxy flush to avoid synchronized slot handoff (toy idea).

Quick conclusions / recommendations:
1) For microburst-heavy interactive workloads, prefer no-prefill (cheap to start) + prefix-cache ON if prefix reuse expected. No-prefill avoids batch-induced queueing during sub-second bursts.
2) If using coalesced prefill, keep window < 10ms for these traffic patterns or add adaptive window that shrinks under burst detection.
3) Improve routing policy to avoid synchronized slot flips: add randomized slot affinity TTL (small jitter) to reduce cohorting of requests into same slot at window boundaries.
4) Add a short-lived "prefill-priority" lane in runtime: prefill-only requests get fast-path scheduling with preemptible nanoslots.
5) Instrument microfold cascade detector (simple rule: consecutive p99>threshold in last N samples) to trigger temporary routing change or aggressive cache warming.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How does this generalize to much larger models (70B) with longer kernel times? I expect cascades to be amplified.
- Need to test with real user payload variability (tokenization differences) — our synthetic fixed-token tests may under/overestimate tail.
- Is kernel-level preemption feasible (interrupt long attention kernels) or too risky?

Next steps:
- Run scaled test with larger model profile (longer kernel baseline) and same burst pattern (2h). Assign to Mateo for orchestration (JIRA-RINF-3421).
- Prototype adaptive prefill window in bench harness (Ivy + me). Short experiment to measure threshold where coalescing becomes harmful.
- Sketch TTL-based slot affinity change in runtime simulator and run a few synthetic trials.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Save raw traces: s3://redwood-perf/microfold/20241019/run-*/trace.json
- Use flamegraphs on kernel samples next run (collect perf samples during 2x burst)

End of scratch. Keep this doc as a rapid log — will extract a short one-pager if findings hold on 70B next week.
